text:
sasha: quick heads-up — saw a perf regression on Qwen-7B mixture when the kernel selector falls back from native fp8 to int8 on a few layers. repro on nightly canary.

rahul: ugh, details? batch size / seq len?

sasha: small batches (1-4), seq len mostly ~64. overall tokens/sec down ~18% and p99 latency up ~35%. not consistent across models — llama/mistral didn't show the same drop.

maria: are we sure it’s the kernel switch and not kv behaviour? did you capture kvcache hit rates?

sasha: yes, ran with --kv-stats. hit rate identical. trace shows selector chose int8 GEMM for attention in some heads after quant-profile mismatch step.

jonathan: can you paste the selector log?

sasha: here, trimmed:
```
[selector] model=qwen-7b quant_profile=fp8_preferred
[selector] layer=attn_kv: prefer_kernel=fp8_gemm score=0.72
[selector] layer=attn_kv: fallback=int8_gemm (compat=1) latency_penalty=+0.12
[selector] chosen=int8_gemm
```

kevin: interesting — score 0.72 and still fell back. that +0.12 penalty looks like our heuristic for fp8 micro-inefficiencies on this hw. maybe the penalty math is tuned from benching on longer sequences.

rahul: ran microbench on same card (A800) with scripts in perf repo. quick numbers:
```
model=qwen-7b seq=64 bs=1
fp8_native: 680 tokens/sec, p99=42ms
int8_fallback: 560 tokens/sec, p99=57ms
```

maria: that matches sasha's numbers. so fallback is worse here. we need the selector to be sensitive to short-seq scenarios.

perf-bot: automated perf snapshot attached — canary #2112. diff: -17% throughput, +33% p99. commit refs: runtime/kernel-selector@c4f2.

jonathan: two hypotheses: (A) calibration for qwen fp8 produced conservative scales causing more Dequant ops or memory loads, hurting small-batch perf; (B) our kernel penalty weights assume amortization from batching. both plausible.

rahul: proposed fix: add a single-shot override that prefers native fp8 for seq_len <= 128 and bs <= 4 unless quant_compat flag explicitly disallows it. simple change in kernel_selector:
```
if (seq_len <= 128 && batch <= 4 && quant_profile == "fp8_preferred") {
  prefer(fp8_native)
}
```

sasha: +1 to that as a fast mitigation. we should also record this scenario in the model-profile metadata so deploys know to prefer fp8 for Qwen.

maria: I'll re-run calibration with a mix of short-context prompts (0.2/0.8 short/long) and generate a new quant table. will post results.

kevin: long-term we should fix kernel penalty math to include an explicit per-op overhead term and kv-cache friendliness. right now it’s mostly steady-state throughput.

jonathan: agree. add a ticket to runtime backlog: "selector: include sequence-length and kvcache overhead in kernel cost model". rahul can you pick up the quick override and a unit test?

rahul: taking it. will push a draft PR today for canary. tag @eng-runtime and @eng-ml.

maria: calibration results (wip): after re-calib, fp8_native throughput 700 tokens/sec, p99=39ms — slight improvement. but quant-quality checks still pass on our eval set.

perf-bot: microbench retest after maria's calib — throughput +3% vs before, overall still +12% behind baseline when selector picks int8.

sasha: plan: 1) rahul: land selector override canary (on small canary fleet) 2) maria: publish new calib and model-profile for qwen-7b 3) kevin/jonathan: backlog ticket for refined cost model 4) perf team: run the usual regression suite for the canary and post results in thread.

jonathan: also flagging that Mistral showed opposite behaviour on same card — it preferred fp8 and was fine. likely model-specific activation distributions. we should keep per-model heuristics rather than global ones.

kevin: agreed — add per-model overrides in model metadata: quant_policy={prefer_fp8, prefer_int8, auto}. start with qwen-7b: prefer_fp8_shortseq.

rahul: PR up: runtime:selector#342 — contains override + unit tests + canary toggle. will run canary tomorrow AM.

maria: posted new quant-profile artifact: artifacts/qwen-7b/fp8_calib-v2.json (internal link). small improvement on short-contexts.

perf-bot: canary run completed: canary fleet (n=8) saw throughput -1% overall, p99 -4% with override enabled. rolling to staging.

sasha: sweet. keep an eye on production telemetry. if regressions pop up revert selector toggle and schedule deeper perf triage.

jonathan: follow-up items for documentation: add a short note in model-profiles.md explaining why qwen has shortseq fp8 preference and how to re-run calib for short contexts.

kevin: filing the docs PR.

rahul: will follow up with numbers once full canary finishes.

maria: if anyone wants the calib script: run `python tools/calib.py --model qwen-7b --short-context-weight 0.8`

sasha: thanks all. good cross-team triage. :thumbsup:
